questions.stem: A patient was stabbed at the level of the manubrium of sternum. Which of the following structures is most likely affected?
A man was stabbed in the neck, 2 cm above the clavicle, and developed pneumothorax. Which of the following structures is most likely injured?
A patient presents with herpes zoster (shingles) lesions at the umbilical region. Which of the following dermatomes corresponds to this region?
45-year-old man has history of hoarseness for 1 month. A chest X-ray shows a mass at aortopulmonary window. Which of following left-sided nerve most likely to be compressed?

A 60-year-old man has worked in a shipyard handling asbestos insulation for 35 years. He presents with fever (38.5°C), productive cough with yellow sputum, and shortness of breath for 3 days. On examination, there are crackles over the right lower lung field. Chest X-ray shows right lower-lobe consolidation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old man presents with a gunshot wound to the right chest. Chest X-ray shows pleural effusion and partial collapse of the right lung. Which of the following is the most likely site for intrapleural fluid accumulation?

A hematoxylin & eosin (H&E)-stained section of lung tissue shows the following features: Simple ciliated columnar epithelium, Abundant smooth muscle and elastic fibers in the lamina propria, No cartilage or submucosal glands Which of the following structures is most likely represented in this section?
A patient is found to have inability of vocal cord abduction. Weakness of which of the following muscles is most likely responsible?
50-years-old man working in a coal mine for 30 years has been persistent cough and increase dyspnea. If a bronchial biopsy brush was done on this man. Which bronchial epithelium would be found?

choices.C: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells

questions.stem: Which of the following muscles, when weakened or paralyzed, leads to impaired vocal cord adduction?

infant presented to the emergency room after respiratory distress. On exam, he was observed to have tachypnea, increased work of breathing, and decreased breath sounds. On chest X-ray, he was found to have a congenital diaphragmatic hernia. Which of these structures fail to develop?
During the first minute of aerobic exercise, ventilation increases rapidly before significant changes in blood gases occur. Which of the following mechanisms is primarily responsible?
In the patient with pulmonary fibrosis experiencing dyspnea, which muscle is actively involved when force expiration?
Which of the following lung volumes or airway parameters is typically higher in an elderly man compared with a young adult man?
During forceful expiration, such as when coughing or exercising, which of the following pressures primarily increases to push air out of the lungs?
A 20-year-old man suffers a rib fracture that penetrates his right pleura. Which of the following is the most likely pathophysiological effect?
Which of the following conditions is most likely to decrease lung compliance?
A person suffers a severe brainstem injury. On examination, they exhibit deep and slow breathing (Bradypnea with large tidal volumes). Which of the following brain areas is most likely affected?
When V/Q ratio of a lung region decreases (i.e., perfusion > ventilation), which of the following changes in alveolar gas tension would you expect?
A healthy adult experiences an increase in arterial CO₂ (hypercapnia). Which of the following responses is most likely?
Which of the following mechanisms is most likely to decrease arterial PO₂ in a patient with asthma?

A preterm infant (28 weeks) presents with tachypnea, grunting, intercostal retractions, and cyanosis. Chest X-ray shows diffuse ground-glass appearance with air bronchograms. Which of the following is the most likely physiological response?

choices.A: Normal tidal volumes with minimal effort
choices.B: Increased work of breathing to maintain minute ventilation
choices.C: Reduced respiratory rate to conserve energy

questions.stem: In an upright, healthy adult, which of the following parameters is higher at the apex of the lung compared to the base?
A 30-year-old man presents with throat pain after swallowing fish. He reports that food passage is painful. Where is the most likely site where the fish bone is lodged?
An X-ray of a patient reveals a tumor located at the floor of the orbit. Which paranasal sinus is the most likely origin of this tumor?
Which of the following causes a decrease in the ventilation/perfusion ratio?
Which form accounts for the majority of CO₂ transport in venous blood?

A newborn presents with excessive drooling, choking, and cyanosis during attempts at feeding. The neonatologist attempts to pass a nasogastric tube, but it cannot be advanced into the stomach. Imaging shows coiling of the tube in the upper esophagus. What is the most likely underlying anatomical defect?

A preterm neonate presents with tachypnea, grunting, and chest retractions shortly after birth. Chest X-ray shows a “ground glass” appearance. The underlying abnormality is most likely due to dysfunction or deficiency of which cells?
In neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), which of the following best describes the consequence of surfactant deficiency in the lungs?

A patient with diabetes mellitus presents with altered ventilation(ketoacidosis). Which of the following receptors is primarily responsible for detecting hypoxemia and mediating increased breathing rate in this patient?

A 60-year-old man presents with acute pulmonary edema. He complains of dyspnea and rapid, shallow breathing. Which of the following receptors is primarily responsible for stimulating this abnormal breathing pattern?

A 30-year-old man develops pulmonary edema after severe hypoxemia. His chest X-ray shows bilateral infiltrates, and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure is normal. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of his pulmonary edema?
In the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve, which of the following conditions increases oxygen-hemoglobin affinity (shifts the curve to the left)?

A 32-year-old man presents with chronic cough, weight loss, and night sweats. Chest X- ray shows upper lobe infiltrates with cavitation. Biopsy of the lung lesion shows granulomatous inflammation. Which of the following cells are typically seen in this condition?

choices.B: Epitheloid cells and Langhans giant cells

questions.stem: A patient is stabbed in the right lower chest. He develops pneumothorax. On chest X- ray, which lung region should be carefully evaluated for collapse or injury?
A 40-year-old man suffers injuries in a car accident. On examination, he is breathing shallowly and slowly. Which of the following respiratory centers is most likely affected?
Which of the following pathologies increases the elastic work of breathing?
In which of the following situations would a healthy person most likely develop an increase in arterial PCO₂?

choices.E: Staying in a high-altitude area for several weeks

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man presents with progressive dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain. Physical examination shows decreased breath sounds and stony dullness on percussion at the right lower lung zone. Pleural effusion is suspected. Which chest X-ray (CXR) view would best demonstrate the presence of pleural effusion?
What called the volume of air remaining in the lungs at the end of normal expiration?
During the respiratory cycle, at which lung volume is airway resistance the lowest?

choices.B: At tidal volume at rest (functional residual capacity, FRC)

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man has a respiratory rate (RR) of 10 breaths/min. His tidal volume (Vt) is such that total ventilation = 8 L/min. The physiological dead space (Vd) is 200 mL. Calculate the alveolar ventilation (Va)
A 60-year-old smoker presents with progressive shortness of breath. Pulmonary function test shows decreased FEV₁ and increased lung compliance. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old girl with severe allergic asthma continues to have frequent exacerbations despite high-dose inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting β2 agonists. Which of the following drugs binds to IgE and prevents it from activating mast cells and basophils?
MOA of 5-LO inhibitor

A 45-year-old man with chronic bronchitis presents with productive cough and difficulty expectorating sputum. The physician prescribes a drug that not only helps liquefy and clear mucus, but also has the ability to stimulate pulmonary surfactant production, improving lung function. Which of the following drugs was most likely prescribed?
A patient has sticky mucus and a productive cough. What medication should be used?
A 30-year-old man with allergic rhinitis uses a topical nasal decongestant spray for several days. Which of the following adverse effects should be monitored or warned about?
Which effect of first-generation H1 antihistamines is responsible for reducing rhinorrhea in common cold?
Regarding antihistamines, if the patient is concerned about sedation, which medication causes the least drowsiness?
A 50-year-old man with COPD has an acute exacerbation with wheezing and dyspnea. After endotracheal intubation, which chest X-ray position is most appropriate to confirm the tube placement?

A 58-year-old man presents with chronic cough and upper chest pain. The physician suspects a Pancoast tumor at the apex of the right lung. Which type of chest X-ray projection is most appropriate to visualize the lung apex clearly?
A 62-year-old male smoker undergoes a chest X-ray. There is a well-defined mass in right upper lobe (indicated by the arrow). What is most likely radiographic density of this mass?
CXR shows obscured right heart border. Where is the pathology located?

A 55-year-old woman with a 30-year history of smoking presents with chronic cough. A bronchial biopsy reveals squamous epithelium with keratin pearls and prominent intercellular bridges. Which of the following is the most likely radiographic pattern of her lung lesion?

choices.E: Central mass and a peripheral nodule

questions.stem: A 65-year-old male with a 40-pack-year smoking history presents with a central lung mass. Biopsy shows small, round blue cells with scant cytoplasm. Immunohistochemistry reveals positivity for a neuroendocrine marker and TTF-1. Which combination of IHC markers is most useful to confirm the diagnosis of small cell lung carcinoma?

A 36-week gestation neonate is born with respiratory distress. Imaging shows the spleen, liver, and intestines herniated into the left thoracic cavity. What is the most likely complication affecting the lungs?

A 2-year-old boy presents with fever, cough, and signs of otitis media. Gram stain of a nasopharyngeal swab shows small Gram-negative coccobacilli. Culture is negative on blood agar but grows on chocolate agar. Which organism is the most likely cause?
A 25-year-old male suffers a traumatic brain injury with a complete transection above the pons. Which of the following is expected?

choices.A: The voluntary control of breathing disappears

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man presents with a history of repeated severe pneumonia since childhood. Chest CT shows marked dilation of the right bronchi. Which of the following best explains the underlying cause of his condition?

choices.B: Goblet cell hyperplasia with excessive mucus secretion
choices.D: Recurrent inflammation with bronchial wall destruction
choices.E: Malignant tumor obstructing the right main bronchus

questions.stem: A 68-year-old presents with fever, chills, and productive cough. Sputum Gram stain shows Gram-positive, lancet-shaped diplococci. Which of the following additional laboratory findings would support the diagnosis?

choices.A: Grows on McConkey agar, oxidase positive
choices.C: Grows on chocolate agar with required X and V factor
choices.D: β-hemolytic colonies on blood agar, bacitracin sensitive
choices.E: α-hemolytic colonies on blood agar, optochin sensitive

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man presents with high fever, productive cough, and pleuritic chest pain. Gram stain of sputum shows Gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci. Colonies are alpha- hemolytic and optochin-sensitive. Most likely causative organism?
A 12-year-old boy presents with high fever, headache, myalgia, sore throat, and cough during flu season. The physician wants to confirm influenza A infection. Which specimen is most appropriate?

choices.A: Nasopharyngeal swab in viral transport medium

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man presents with high fever, cough, and progressive dyspnea. He reports that during the past 2 weeks, several chickens he raised at home have died suddenly. Avian influenza infection is suspected. Which of the following is the most appropriate specimen for laboratory confirmation of the diagnosis?
A chest X-ray shows a well-defined mass in the right middle lobe of the lung. Which of the following best describes the radiographic density of this lesion?
Which of the following cells is the major source of interleukin-5 (IL-5), a cytokine that plays an important role in eosinophil activation and proliferation?
A patient undergoes venous blood sampling, and air accidentally enters the syringe. Which of the following changes is expected in the measured arterial blood gas?
A patient presents with sudden dyspnea, hemoptysis, and hypoxemia after blunt chest trauma. Chest X-ray shows diffuse alveolar infiltrates. Which of the following best describes the site of bleeding?

A 40-year-old man presents with fever, productive cough, dyspnea, and inspiratory crepitations on chest auscultation. Chest X-ray reveals consolidation in the right lower lobe. Which of the following is the main mechanism leading to hypoxemia in this patient?

choices.A: Increased diffusion capacity of the lung
choices.C: Increased pulmonary capillary perfusion without ventilation
choices.D: Decreased V/Q ratio (V/Q mismatch due to shunt-like effect)
choices.E: Decreased oxygen consumption in the tissues

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man has recurrent spontaneous pneumothorax. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause?

A 30-year-old man presents with fever, weight loss, and chronic cough. Chest X-ray shows a cavitary lesion, and sputum is AFB-positive (3+). Which of the following immune mechanisms is most important for controlling this organism?

A 4-year-old boy is brought to the emergency room after accidentally ingesting petroleum oil. Physical examination shows bilateral crepitations, nasal flaring, and hypoxemia (SaO₂ = 90%). After administering 100% oxygen, the hypoxemia persists. Which of the following mechanisms best explains the hypoxemia in this patient?

choices.C: Alveolar collapse and surfactant inactivation (intrapulmonary shunt)

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with sudden shortness of breath and anxiety. ABG: pH 7.48, PaCO₂ 28 mmHg, HCO₃⁻ 24 mEq/L. What is the primary acid-base disorder?

A 25-year-old man with type 1 diabetes mellitus presents to the emergency room with nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and fatigue for the past 2 days. He reports polyuria and polydipsia. On examination, he is tachypneic with deep, rapid respirations. Laboratory findings show: glucose 450 mg/dL,Serum ketones: positive, ABG: pH 7.33, PaCO₂ 28 mmHg, HCO₃⁻ 15 mEq/L. Which of the following best describes his primary acid-base disorder?

A 32-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with sudden onset of shortness of breath, chest pain, palpitations, and dizziness after receiving news of a family emergency. She is anxious, restless, and breathing rapidly at 30 breaths/min. Physical examination reveals no cyanosis and clear lung sounds. ABG shows: pH 7.51, PaCO₂ 28 mmHg, HCO₃⁻23 mEq/L. Which of the following is the most likely acid-base disorder?

A 65-year-old man with chronic bronchitis presents with progressive dyspnea. Arterial blood gas shows PaO₂ 60 mmHg, PaCO₂ 40 mmHg. He is given supplemental oxygen, and his PaO₂ improves significantly. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism of his hypoxemia?
A 3-year-old child with cyanotic congenital heart disease presents with low oxygen saturation despite oxygen therapy. Which mechanism best explains the hypoxemia?

A 35-year-old man is brought to the emergency room after a car accident. He has multiple rib fractures involving several adjacent ribs. On physical examination, the chest wall moves inward during inspiration and outward during expiration. Which of the following best explains this paradoxical chest wall movement?

choices.A: Flail chest due to multiple rib fractures

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman accidentally aspirates a peanut while laughing. On chest examination, decreased breath sounds are noted on the right lower lung field. Which of the following anatomic characteristics best explains why aspirated foreign bodies are more likely to lodge in the right lower lobe bronchus?

choices.A: Right main bronchus is longer and more horizontal than the left
choices.B: Right main bronchus is narrower and more curved than the left
choices.C: Right main bronchus is shorter, wider, and more vertical than the left
choices.D: Left main bronchus is shorter and wider than the right
